scope: September 8 manifest reconciliation: all 16 official downloads match their manifest fingerprints and existing catalog records. Fresh review of the 15 PDFs and eleven-sheet workbook adds LDFA, intermediate-aquifer map and Cadillac biosolids tie-backs. A subsequent three-PDF review adds the 2022 N3862 report's early-2019 injection statement to the transition evidence. The 2020 LDFA minutes and signed 2015 air-inspection scan add historical context, not missing analytical or leachate transaction packages. All 23 requirement dispositions were checked; this is not a fresh reread of the whole repository.
note: All 16 manifest documents are already accounted for; repeat downloads do not create new records. The later batch adds one LDFA record and a materially distinct signed inspection version, retaining one exact staff-report duplicate under its existing record. These additions close no additional request. One local construction/lithology requirement remains satisfied, with 22 requests still open. Missing tickets, missing documents doesn’t mean missing events.

blocks.summary: Actual leachate offloading and the landfill–WWTP relationship are documented. Seven requests remain for individual transactions, signed agreements and the exact cessation date.

held.finding: The signed September 19, 1995 Missaukee–Wexford DPW solid-waste disposal agreement requires authorized commercial-hauler lists and provides for tipping fees on delivery, with fees separately set by resolution.
held.limitation: This agreement concerns solid waste into Wexford landfill, not the 2009 Wexford–Cadillac leachate-treatment agreement. No numerical rate schedule, actual payments, individual loads or signed later renewals are supplied.

held.finding: Wexford’s April 19, 2011 approval and May 1, 2012 amendment document changing import/export conditions. American Waste’s May 14, 2014 Lake County request is followed by DEQ approval August 31, 2016.
held.limitation: These concern solid waste authorized into the landfill, not actual leachate deliveries from it to Cadillac WWTP. Planning authorization is not a receiving log, invoice, fee payment or evidence of a final leachate delivery.

held.finding: January 12, 2016: the City letter documents actual American Waste leachate offloading and a spill at Cadillac WWTP. Missing tickets do not negate this documented activity.
held.limitation: 9:22 a.m. is the notification-call time; 10,000 gallons is tanker capacity, not a measured load or spill. The typed letter does not identify the originating landfill.

held.finding: A February 3, 2011 inspection entry describes County Landfill leachate received at the equalization tank. The SIU profile reports Wexford County Landfill wastewater averaging 33,000 gallons per day, intermittently. November 2017 City minutes describe landfill liquid hauled to the WWTP and payment for treatment.
held.limitation: The 2011 observation falls within the requested 2009–July 2019 period but does not provide a continuous receiving series. The SIU page has no printed date (2017 comes from file metadata); its average is not an individual delivery quantity. These are not per-load logs or receipts.

held.finding: September 8, 2009: motion 2009.216 approves the leachate-treatment arrangement for July 1, 2009–June 30, 2011 and identifies Miscellaneous File No. 842.
held.limitation: Approval minutes are held; the fully executed agreement, signed numerical rate schedule and later signed renewals are still needed. Item_149.pdf is the same approval-minutes original. The separately supplied filename 842.pdf contains January 19, 2016 Council minutes, not Miscellaneous File No. 842.

held.finding: March 18, 2019: the City expected leachate revenue to end when the injection well went online. June 28: Cadillac reports the landfill moved to deep-well injection and told the City it would no longer bring leachate. December 18: the IPP report states “No longer accepting leachate” and reports deep-well injection. The August 15, 2022 N3862 staff report separately states that injection began in early 2019 (p4).
held.limitation: This is affirmative City-reported transition/cessation context with later agency history, not the exact effective cessation date or final receiving-log entry. Beginning injection does not by itself establish when all off-site hauling stopped.

held.finding: May 2016 budget material pursues additional hauled-waste revenue alongside pollution-control goals and reports above-budget leachate revenue. The May 2017 DEQ FAQ identifies alternative shipping/receipt records and generator, transporter and receiving-facility custodians.
held.limitation: Aggregate revenue is not a delivery-linked invoice or ledger. The FAQ is historical guidance, not a completed shipping record, proof records still exist, or a statement of current law.

held.finding: 2015 and April 2017 County minutes preserve Cedar Creek record-access and fee-discussion comments. November 2017 County minutes direct preparation of an injection-well opposition resolution. EPA’s 2017–2018 fact sheets and draft permit document the proposed alternative.
held.limitation: Public comments, a resolution-preparation vote and draft permitting do not supply executed treatment agreements, original billing, operational injection records or a final Cadillac delivery date.

held.finding: The October 2020 Executive packet contains RAP budget invoice references, a proposal to bring contaminated soil to Wexford landfill, and a separate Cedar Creek drinking-water sampling requirement.
held.limitation: These are not original leachate invoices, proof of payment, completed soil deliveries, Cadillac WWTP deliveries or completed PFAS tests.

held.finding: October 18 and November 1, 2010: City minutes record American Waste landfill-sale discussions and Council approval of the 2009 Solid Waste Management Plan amendment by 3–2. November’s minutes correct the earlier discussion to future flow-control options and describe anticipated closure/post-closure obligations and required relocation of trash from an unlined cell.
held.limitation: These are solid-waste governance records within the requested 2009–July 2019 period, not wastewater-flow logs, proof of a completed sale or relocation, leachate receipts, or the executed treatment agreement.

held.finding: City budgets report $2,996,632 in FY2011–FY2019 Actual Leachate revenue. FY2018 actual $431,105 reconciles to amended budget $400,000 plus $31,105; FY2019 actual $494,691 matches the $450,000 exhibit plus $44,691.
held.limitation: Annual account totals do not identify every payer or delivery. FY2017 retains a $1 variance discrepancy; FY2016’s comparable final budget and FY2019’s corrected executed amendment remain unresolved. Delivery-linked invoices, receipts, ledgers, signed treatment agreements and the exact final delivery remain needed. MD&A statements are not independently audited receipts.

blocks.followUp: Seek the 2009–July 2019 generator, hauler and Cadillac receiving records, and reconcile surviving delivery rows to City receivables and landfill billing. Use Miscellaneous File No. 842 to locate the signed 2009 agreement/rate schedule and later renewals. Seek the last receiving entry or dated operational cessation notice to resolve the March–June–December 2019 sequence; do not infer an exact last load from it. Separately, pursue Missaukee hauler rosters supplied to Wexford DPW under the 1995 agreement §2.3, related tipping-fee resolutions/payment records under §§4.1–4.2 and executed renewals. Keep these upstream landfill records separate from Cadillac leachate transactions.

blocks.summary: Verified records establish PFAS in leachate, WWTP effluent and a separate digester/sludge sampling round, alongside equipment purchasing and installation. All three requests remain for matched main-WWTP influent, effluent and biosolids samples with corresponding operating logs.

held.finding: The JWC quotation, April 2016 award of $52,100 for JWC equipment and two HESCO samplers, and February 2023 minutes corroborating installation in 2016 establish distinct quotation, authorization and installation evidence.
held.limitation: The quotation gives estimated lead times, not an actual shipment date or carrier. Retrospective installation evidence does not supply the requested synchronized PFAS sampling or operating logs.

held.finding: Minutes document the Kemira ferric-chloride purchasing extension through December 2017, Webb’s 2018–2020 contract at $0.245 per dry pound, and a $9,300 award for three Mattoon & Lee WWTP pumps.
held.limitation: These are purchasing authorizations, not individual delivery receipts or measurements of PFAS treatment performance.

held.finding: The June 2019 source-status form reports outfall PFOS and PFOA results but explicitly marks influent sampling “NO” for that reporting period. This is a specific reporting-period statement, not proof that influent was never sampled.
held.limitation: The form’s source-status selection does not mean zero effluent PFOS or demonstrate treatment-removal efficiency. LDFA influent is not main-WWTP influent. Sample timestamps and the single 2 MGD value are not time-of-day operator and flow logs.

held.finding: October 3, 2018 leachate sampling reports primary PFOS 120 and PFOA 590 ng/L, with duplicate results of 140 and 700 ng/L. The source report preserves separate sample identities and laboratory context.
held.limitation: Leachate-source chemistry is not mixed main-WWTP influent. These samples are not synchronized with the later effluent or digester round; they cannot establish a treatment-removal percentage.

held.finding: The laboratory tables and chain of custody document Digester #4 primary/duplicate sampling on December 26, 2018 at 13:35. This independently supports PFAS testing of the sludge/digester stream.
held.limitation: The covering email says December 27; the laboratory tables and custody record say December 26. The lab reports Water/ng/L with estimated values and matrix-interference qualifications. Do not relabel these as directly reported dry-weight concentrations or a paired influent/effluent/biosolids round.

held.finding: The statewide report’s Table 3 lists Cadillac WWTP effluent PFAS results for November 2018, June 2019 and October 2019, corroborating a repeated effluent record.
held.limitation: Those Cadillac rows do not supply main-WWTP influent, synchronized sludge/biosolids measurements or the matching operating logs. Separate sampling dates and matrices are not a paired treatment study.

sources.label: Cadillac effluent rows · Table 3, PDF p83

held.finding: LDFA Special Investigation tables identify I-5 Influent 50385014001 and I-5 Effluent 50385014002/003 collected October 14, 2024. Influent PFOA/PFOS are 5.9/2.4 ppt; effluent and duplicate are each <2.0/<2.0 ppt. These are same-calendar-date LDFA entries, not established main-WWTP samples.
held.limitation: No exact sampling times, hydraulic pairing, synchronized sludge/biosolids, operating logs or complete field/custody/QC package is supplied. Do not calculate main-WWTP removal efficiency. A15/A17 duplicate A13 pages 22/24, not independent corroboration. For November 18, 2024 samples 2411198-01/-02/-03, A18 prints analysis November 27, 2025 where A16/A17 print 2024; retain the unresolved date conflict.

held.finding: EGLE’s May 2025 FAQ includes Cadillac-specific biosolids results under Land Application Years: PFOS/PFOA 5.1/2.3 ppb for 2024 and 3.5/3.5 ppb for 2025; the 2021–2023 bounds are <5.5, <6.3 and <7.5 for both analytes. EGLE then stated it had no evidence of industrially impacted biosolids applied locally or land application as a groundwater-contamination source in this area.
held.limitation: Blank Cadillac 2018 cells are missing, not nondetects; censored bounds are not zero. The table supplies no sample IDs, collection times, custody/QC package or paired influent/effluent/sludge round. Preserve EGLE’s statement as its May 2025 assessment, not categorical exclusion of all historical releases or pathways.

sources.label: Cadillac biosolids table and agency assessment · A24 pp4–5

blocks.followUp: Seek native main-WWTP influent PFAS reports first, then align sample IDs and collection times with effluent and sludge/biosolids results, full QC and corresponding operator/flow logs. Keep leachate-source, LDFA, effluent and digester records separate until a documented pairing exists. Obtain the original I-5 work-order reports, sample-point definitions, timestamps and QC, and resolve the conflicting analysis year for samples 2411198-01/-02/-03. Seek the underlying Cadillac biosolids laboratory reports summarized in the May 2025 FAQ; do not join different media by year alone.

blocks.summary: Already satisfied: local well-construction and lithology records. The remaining four requests concern the specific Plett well and measured local groundwater conditions; regional or delivery context does not complete them.

held.finding: The February 2007 CTI facility map locates boundaries and landfill cells. The separate November 5, 2013 Golder map depicts wells and leachate infrastructure, including a 20,000-gallon backup tank.
held.limitation: Repeated CTI pages are the same map. Neither figure supplies surveyed synoptic water levels, local hydraulic-test results or a source-to-Plett groundwater-flow map; infrastructure depiction is not actual flow or delivery proof.

held.finding: The official Wexford Wellogic package supplies local construction and lithology data; the existing review identified 45 wells with linked lithology within 1,000 meters of the geocoded 1121 Plett point.
held.limitation: This prior closure does not supply the certified 1140 Plett record, surveyed synoptic elevations/water levels, hydraulic tests or a source-to-Plett groundwater-flow map.

held.finding: The February 26, 2025 MPART update includes AECOM Figure 4 dated February 24, 2025: a PFAS criteria map with groundwater-flow arrows using existing intermediate-aquifer data and approximate historic LDFA/Rexair capture zones. It supplies local directional context beyond a generic regional map.
held.limitation: The figure does not identify 1140 Plett, provide surveyed hydraulic heads, contours or water-level measurement dates, or demonstrate a source-to-Plett connection. Page 27 labels the aquifer diagram an example rather than an accurate rendering; flow varies by aquifer. Intermediate-aquifer arrows do not establish flow in every aquifer or PFAS source attribution.

sources.label: Existing-data flow map and aquifer caveat · A20 pp27–30

blocks.followUp: Use the held local well inventory to identify candidate wells, then seek the certified 1140 Plett completion/screen record, surveyed wellhead elevations, one dated synoptic water-level round, identified-well hydraulic tests and a site-specific source-to-Plett flow map. Construction data alone cannot establish gradient or travel direction. Request the underlying AECOM existing-data basis for Figure 4, including surveyed elevations, dated heads, aquifer/screen assignments and capture-zone assumptions, then determine whether it can be extended to the identified Plett receptor.

blocks.summary: Repeated Plett analytical results and a 24-page mixed-source packet are held. Selected EGLE work-order pages are only part of that packet. The complete 49-page original and three sample-specific custody/field records remain requested.

held.finding: The 24-page mixed-source packet preserves the September 10, 2025 side-by-side results, selected EGLE Work Order 2509147 pages, Merit/Cyclopure material and an EGLE letter. Its first-page comparison table identifies the initial Cyclopure collection date as March 7, 2025, consistent with the original report rather than its March 4 filename.
held.limitation: The packet is not 24 of the 49 work-order pages: it combines different records, so subtracting 24 from 49 does not establish how many work-order pages are missing. The complete work order and separate sample-specific custody/field sheets are still needed.

sources.label: Mixed-source packet · comparison p1; selected EGLE pages pp2–9

blocks.followUp: Seek the complete original 49-page EGLE Work Order 2509147 rather than another copy of the mixed-source packet. Seek sample-specific custody/field records for March 7, 2025 (kit WTK_PFAS_16874; 09:30 printed, timezone unspecified), September 10, 2025 and April 9, 2026. Preserve March 4 as an original filename alias, not the sampling date.

blocks.summary: AOI results, maps and the comparability study provide context, not a completed source-to-receptor attribution package. All four confirmation requests remain open.

held.finding: The complete MPART comparability study and 26-page EGLE results compilation are held. The fresh manifest review confirms A14–A18 are standalone copies of A13 pages 21–26, while AOI address numbering restarts between collection rounds; repeated views are not additional samples.
held.limitation: The study is not a PFAS source investigation. Anonymized address/LDFA results do not replace a source/receptor coordinate crosswalk, an explicit transect, synchronized source samples or matching field/QC records. A13 page 19 has an undated, unnumbered TBA column; it must not be counted as a verified sample. Named field blanks in table notes are not a complete blank-results/QC package.

blocks.followUp: Seek a documented upgradient/cross-gradient/downgradient sampling plan, a complete source/receptor coordinate-to-sample-ID table, one synchronized source/receptor sampling round and its field/QC package. AOI maps and receptor comparability results guide the search but do not establish source attribution. Seek the original address/sample crosswalk and field-blank reports before joining numbered addresses across rounds; do not treat heat-map dates as shared sampling dates.
